transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love—my workshop, church, even fishing don’t mean anything to me right now. I just can't seem to find the interest or energy for any of it anymore.
Have you had similar periods of depression or loss of interest before, or did this start after a specific stressful life event?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like this before. It all started about three weeks ago, right after my doctor raised concerns about mild cognitive impairment, ordered memory tests, and told me to cut back on driving. That was a massive blow to my independence and my whole identity as an engineer, and I've just spiraled since then.

Since this started, have you been feeling down or hopeless most of the day nearly every day, along with changes like poor sleep, appetite, concentration, or feelings of worthlessness? Or does it feel more like distress mainly tied to the news about your memory and driving?

It definitely started with the news about my memory and driving, but now it has evolved into a constant, daily struggle. Most days I feel this heavy, hollow ache in my chest and have barely any appetite, just getting by on coffee and toast. My mind also feels incredibly foggy and hard to focus, which just makes me feel completely useless.

Even when you’re not thinking about the memory concerns or driving, do the low mood and loss of interest stay there most of the day? Or do they mainly get worse when you’re focused on that specific situation?

Yes, it's there all the time, even when I'm not actively thinking about my memory or driving. It's like a constant, heavy, hollow ache in my chest that just stays in the background of everything I do. Even if my wife tries to distract me, I still can't find any interest or joy in anything and just want to stay in my chair.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about yourself, beyond just being upset about the memory and driving changes? If so, is that feeling present most days?
I wouldn't say I feel excessive guilt or a general sense of worthlessness. But I do feel pretty useless lately, specifically because I struggle so much with simple decisions and my memory these days.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself? If yes, have you had any plan or intent to act on them?

Sometimes, especially at night when the house is quiet, I do find myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I hate the thought of my wife having to watch me fall apart like this. But I don't have any plans or intent to actually hurt myself.

Since this began, have there been any periods of a few hours or more when your mood noticeably lifts and you can enjoy things if something good happens or you’re distracted? Or has the depression stayed about the same no matter what is going on?

No, it stays about the same and doesn't really lift at all. Even when my wife tries to encourage me by saying the guys at church or the kids from the maker space are asking for me, I just feel completely numb. I don't feel any excitement or curiosity, so I just make an excuse and stay in my chair.

Since this started, has it become hard to manage basic daily tasks like getting dressed, showering, eating regular meals, or keeping up with chores? Or are you still able to do those things even though you feel miserable?

It has become incredibly difficult to manage even basic tasks; it takes me forever just to get dressed and I can barely keep up with simple chores. I struggle to eat proper meals because fixing them feels like too much effort, so I now have to rely heavily on my wife to remind me to eat, take my medications, and pay the bills on time.

Have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true, such as that you are ruined, being punished, or causing harm? Even if it sounds strange, have any thoughts like that come up during this depression?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't hear or see things that aren't there, and I don't have any beliefs about being ruined or punished. I do, however, worry a great deal about my memory and what is happening to my mind.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms: persistent depressed mood and marked loss of interest nearly all day every day for about 3 weeks, with neurovegetative symptoms (poor appetite, low energy/psychomotor slowing implied by difficulty initiating tasks), impaired concentration, passive death wishes, and clear functional impairment in basic daily activities. Although onset followed a psychosocial stressor, the syndrome has become pervasive, non-reactive, and severe enough to exceed adjustment disorder; no psychotic symptoms are present.
